module purpose: neorv32_hwspinlock implements 32 one-bit lock registers behind a bus request/response interface. It decodes an addressed lock index, updates the selected lock bit with `not bus_req_i.rw` on accesses with `bus_req_i.addr(7)='0'`, returns either the selected bit or the full lock vector on qualified reads, and generates an acknowledge with no error.

use-case flows.value: the selected lock bit is updated to `not bus_req_i.rw` when `bus_req_i.stb='1'`, `bus_req_i.addr(7)='0'`, and the decoded selector matches
on `bus_req_i.stb='1'` and `bus_req_i.rw='0'`, response data returns either `lock_q and sel` when `bus_req_i.addr(7)='0'` or the full `lock_q` vector otherwise
the response acknowledges the request and reports no error
all lock bits are cleared and the response record is forced to `rsp_terminate_c` while `rstn_i='0'`

conceptual assets.concept: Stored spinlock state of the 32 lock bits
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each generated lock process clears `lock_q(i)` on reset (line 42) and, on the clocked update, writes the selected bit with `not bus_req_i.rw` under the addressed-access guard at lines 44-45. The read-out flow depends on the same stored state, returning either `lock_q and sel` (line 68) or the full `lock_q` vector (line 70). Integrity is established because both the lock-update flow and the returned status become incorrect if the stored lock bits do not follow those update and reset rules; availability is also established because the register holds the state between accesses and supplies it to the read path. The readback exit is on excluded transport port `bus_rsp_o`, so the internal store is the eligible structural reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Selected-lock decode decision for addressed accesses
conceptual assets.reasoning: `sel(i)` is computed as a one-hot decode from `bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2)` at line 51. That decision controls which lock bit can update in the lock flow through the guard at line 44 and which bit is returned on addressed read-out through `lock_q and sel` at line 68. Integrity is established because an incorrect selector would update or report the wrong lock bit; availability is also established because line 51 defines the selector whenever an address is presented. The bus address itself enters through excluded transport port `bus_req_i`, so the internal computed selector is the eligible structural reference.
